newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bourse drops probe, BHF Bank to pay costs.
newsitem.headline: German bourse drops probe, BHF Bank to pay costs.

text.p: Frankfurt bourse supervisors on Wednesday said they had shelved an investigation into alleged share price irregularities after the bank at the centre of the probe, BHF Bank AG, offered to pay compensation and an unspecified amount of related costs.
The probe concerned an incident on April 15, when BHF dealers offered Allianz AG shares at unusually low prices on the cash market and then bought Allianz options at knockdown prices.
BHF has agreed to pay out 365,600 marks ($193,000) in compensation to the sellers of the options and carry the costs of the probe which began in late April.
The bourse said in a statement the investigation had been terminated because the case was not significant enough to pursue, especially since BHF had agreed to repay the damage.
However it said investigators had concluded that BHF had acted "thoughtlessly", had breached the trust of other market participants and put them at a financial disadvantage.
BHF said its dealers had not broken bourse rules.
"BHF welcomes the abandonment of the procedure," it said.
"It stresses that it was not its aim to disadvantage other market participants."
